text: It's tempting to open SSMS right now and start hunting for the problem. That's exactly the mistake a real DBA avoids. Jumping straight to CREATE INDEX or rewriting a query before scoping the problem wastes real time fixing something that might not even be the actual bottleneck. Before touching a single DMV, write down the plan.

Two triage questions come first. Is this one query, or the whole system? Both departments reporting slowness at the same time of day, against the same database, points toward something shared. And is this new, or has it always been this way? Neither department said this just started — both described an ongoing, every-morning pattern, which makes more than one real cause more likely, not less.

Here's the five-step plan for this chapter. Identify active sessions: what's actually running right now, during the reported slow window. Find the slow queries: which specific queries are consuming the most time. Read the plan: for the worst offender, what is the execution plan actually doing. Diagnose: missing index, blocking, or both. Fix, then re-test, to confirm with a new plan that it actually worked.

A simpler plan — just add an index everywhere it might help — looks faster but isn't. Indexes aren't free: every one of them slows down every insert, update, and delete, so adding one without evidence can make writes slower while barely helping the real bottleneck. And this investigation turns up more than one real cause, not just one.

Lesson 3 starts Step 1 for real: querying sys dot dm_exec_sessions and sys dot dm_exec_requests to see exactly what's running during the reported mid-morning window. Have SSMS or Azure Data Studio connected to OverlookClinicalDB and ready to run a query — the next several lessons build directly on each other's results.
